Before I give you the exact sequence, I want you to see why we use simple moving averages,
how the same visual language travels across chart timeframes, and where the pattern sits
inside the broad price cycle. That gives us one decision language we can recognize,
execute, and review repeatedly. So why build the framework around moving averages? After working
with many indicators and price patterns, I found that simple moving averages like 10, 20, 50,
and 200 simple moving averages give me enough structure without hiding price. They are calculated
from price, they are widely available on common charting platforms and they recalculate for the
chart time frame you select. Together they give me a simple visual reference for recent direction
and momentum. They also make three conditions easier to see. Price can move through the recent
trend structure, price can return towards that structure, price can become visibly extended from
it. The moving averages do not predict the next candle. For me, their job is very simple. Organize
what price is already doing. They keep my attention on the relationship between price,
the recent trend, and the consolidation that is forming. The moving averages provide the visual
trend area but the actual entry will come from a break in price structure which we will define
after the cycle overview in my own process extra indicators added more decisions without improving
the core read that is why the simple moving averages became the common visual language for
this entire system the same framework can be practiced across different trading time frames
a short-term trader can read it on the intraday chart a swing trader can use a daily chart
position trader can use a weekly chart an investor can use the structure as a technical
timing and management lens alongside fundamental research the chart interval and the speed of the
sequence changes but the operating sequence remains consistent choose the chart that matches
the decision you are trying to make. Once the sequence begins, keep the chart, time frame,
session and moving average settings fixed until the complete opposite sequence provides the final
technical exit. When I call this framework universal, I mean that the same analysis structure
can travel across chart timeframes. It does not mean every chart contains a trade,
every instrument is suitable or every valid pattern makes money, the pattern still requires
meaningful, obvious structure, liquidity, spreads, volatility, account risk, and whether to take a
valid signal belong to the separate trading decision. And sometimes the right trading decision
is to pass even when the chart signal exists. Before we study the three system steps,
look at the broad consolidation to expansion path. Price often alternates between periods
of consolidation and expansion. Stage 1 is consolidation after a decline. Stage 2 is
expansion up. Stage three is consolidation after an advance. Stage four is expansion down. Then the
process can begin again. I use the word consolidation or balance as per auction market
theory. Instead of assuming that every lower base is accumulation or every upper base is distribution,
balance is what we can see we can obviously see consolidation and price moves from consolidation
to expansion from balance to imbalance and back to the balance we cannot know the direction of
the next expansion until price resolves the structure these stages have no fixed duration
and they rarely look perfect.
